newsitem.title: ITALY: Mamma's boy won't take "no" for an answer.
newsitem.headline: Mamma's boy won't take "no" for an answer.

text.p: A 24-year-old Italian has won the right to live with his mother after she threw him out and changed the locks, La Repubblica newspaper reported on Monday.
It said the unmarried man, named in the report only as Luca, took his case to court in Ferrara, northern Italy, after his mother Anna Maria decided he was making her life a misery.
The judge, Francesco Salzano, ruled that the son had a legal right to live with his mother even though he was an adult and had his own income as a petrol pump attendant, the daily said.
The parties to the family row were unavailable for comment but La Repubblica said the mother, 46, was determined to appeal.
"If he comes home then I'm off," it quoted the woman, who is separated from her husband, as saying.
The newspaper used the case to illustrate the "mammismo", or clinging attachment men have to their mothers, that still prevails in Italy.
Nearly 52 percent of Italian males aged 25 to 35 still lived with one or both parents, compared with under 29 percent for women, it said.
"There is something profoundly sick in a society of eternal bambini (children) who love only their mothers," commentator Curzio Maltese wrote in La Repubblica.
